subject: physics
title: Speed
summary: Speed is how fast something is going — the distance it covers divided by the time it takes. Run 100 m in 20 s and your speed is 5 meters every second. Speed is a scalar: it has a size (5 m/s) but no direction. Explore how a motion sensor charts speed on a graph and how 'average' and 'instant' speed differ.

compareCandidate.label: Speed vs. velocity
compareCandidate.description: Speed only tells you how fast (like 80 km/h). Velocity tells you how fast AND which way (like 80 km/h north). A car on a round track can have a constant speed but a constantly changing velocity.

plainLanguageExplanation: Speed tells you how fast something is moving — how much distance it covers in a unit of time. It's a simple ratio: speed = distance / time. If a cyclist rides 60 km in 2 hours the speed is 60/2 = 30 km/h. The standard physics unit is meters per second (m/s). Speed is a scalar, meaning it has size but no direction. There are two flavors: average speed (total distance / total time — what you compute at the end), and instant speed (the needle on a car's speedometer right now). A car that stops at every light can average 30 km/h over the trip even though it hits 60 km/h between lights, showing average is the whole trip while instant is the moment. Graphs of distance vs. time rise at a steady rate (fixed slope) when speed is constant — the steeper the slope line, the faster you're going.

keyFacts.label: Scalar
keyFacts.value: Has size but NO direction — 30 km/h is complete by itself

keyFacts.label: Average speed
keyFacts.value: Total distance ÷ total time, all stops included

keyFacts.label: Instant speed
keyFacts.value: The speed at a single moment — what a speedometer shows

keyFacts.label: Graph shape
keyFacts.value: A constant speed is a straight slanting line on a distance-time graph

whyItMatters: Speed is the number behind almost every trip: how fast a sprinter, a delivery driver, or a satellite moves. It's the classic classroom formula — speed = distance ÷ time — the one most-used equation outside school. Knowing the difference between average and instant speed explains why speed cameras don't just care how far you got, but how fast at a single moment. Speed also paves the road to velocity, acceleration, forces, and energy — the rest of mechanics.
didYouKnow: The speedometer was invented in the late 1800s, and the fastest car on land has topped 1228 km/h. But even fast is relative: the International Space Station circles Earth at about 28,000 km/h — more than 20 times that — yet astronauts onboard feel perfectly still.
compareReason: Speed is the scalar twin of velocity — showing the same trip as 'fast, no direction' vs 'fast, northward' makes the vector versus scalar split instantly visible.
